source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide the direction and speed of air flow from a pressure difference.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: high-pressure region is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: The two air regions must be connected by a path through which air can move.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Air flows from lower pressure toward higher pressure.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when The two air regions must be connected by a path through which air can move is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Air flows from a region of higher pressure to a region of lower pressure; the flow continues until the pressures become almost equal, and a larger pressure difference gives faster air flow. A pressure difference starts air moving from high pressure toward low pressure; reducing the difference slows and stops the flow, while increasing the difference increases the speed. The learner predicts that air flows from higher pressure to lower pressure and that a larger pressure difference produces faster flow. Wind is moving air that chooses a direction by how hard it was first pushed, not by high and low air pressure regions.
